title: Swe mid scenario flaky tests
question: Your CI test suite has become unreliable, tests fail intermittently and rerunning usually makes them pass. How do you approach fixing this?
idealAnswer:
Identifies that flaky tests usually stem from a small set of root causes: shared mutable state between tests, timing/ordering assumptions, unmocked network calls, or reliance on real time/randomness without seeding

Proposes a systematic way to find the worst offenders rather than guessing, e.g. tracking failure rates per test over time or running suspect tests repeatedly in isolation to reproduce the flake

Distinguishes between fixing the root cause (e.g. properly isolating test state, mocking time/network) versus just adding retries, and explains retries are a mitigation, not a fix, they can mask real bugs

Addresses the team/process angle: quarantining known-flaky tests so they don't block unrelated PRs while still tracking and fixing them, rather than letting 'just rerun it' become the norm

Bonus: mentions the deeper cost of tolerating flakiness, teams stop trusting red CI runs and start ignoring real failures too
